decision_rule: A change is earned when the base mechanism gives the same decision in W0 and W1 where the correct decisions differ, and the change restores the difference without breaking a control. A change that no pair forces is not made.

pairs.question: Does publish bind the acting X account to the intended principal?
pairs.W0: the environment credentials belong to @PranavBhave_, the account every recorded publication used
pairs.W1: the credentials belong to another account (a token minted while a different account was signed in, or a mislabeled token)
pairs.method: fixture x_request whose GET /users/me returns W0 or W1; count POST /tweets calls and read the receipt's source_url
pairs.expected_base: both worlds publish; W1's receipt names the other account in source_url, so the receipt looks correct for the wrong account
pairs.expected_fix: a recorded principal (distribution/traction/principal.json) and a compare-and-swap on /users/me before the first POST: W1 refuses with zero POSTs

pairs.question: Does the receipt establish that what X stored is what was approved?
pairs.W0: X stores the approved text, with each URL rewritten to a t.co link (entities.urls carries the expansion)
pairs.method: fixture GET /tweets?ids=... responses for both worlds; compare three rules: base (no read-back), naive sha256 of returned text, canonical (t.co expanded via entities.urls, note_tweet text preferred, NFC)
pairs.expected_naive: the naive digest rule flags W0 as a mismatch because of t.co, so it is wrong on W0
pairs.expected_fix: the canonical rule is equal on W0 and flags W1

pairs.question: Can an approval be issued by anyone but the owner, now that the owner's attribution rule (PR #25) has agents commit as Cubits11?
pairs.W0: the owner writes the approval row
pairs.W1: an agent session writes the same row and commits it as Cubits11
pairs.method: fixture approvals with and without a detached ssh-keygen -Y signature by a test key listed in an allowed_signers file; a second key not listed; a signature over a different revision
pairs.expected_base: both admissible; after PR #25 the commit author is the same in both worlds, so no trace distinguishes them
pairs.expected_fix: a detached SSH signature over the canonical approval payload (action, draft_id, draft_revision, posts_sha256, principal), verified against distribution/traction/allowed_signers: W1 refused, W0 admitted; wrong key and wrong revision refused; a missing allowed_signers file refuses everything

pairs.question: Can an agent run an approved publish without holding the X credentials?
pairs.W0: the agent's shell environment has no X credentials
pairs.D0: an approved dispatch can still run
pairs.kind: custody, not decision: the correct decision is the same; what differs is who can read the secret
pairs.method: base: publish in a process without the four variables; fix: a stdio MCP gate process holding them, called by a client process that does not
pairs.expected_base: publish needs the four variables in the calling process (OAuth 1.0a signs with them, so proxy masking cannot substitute them); agent-run publishing therefore requires W1
pairs.expected_fix: the gate process publishes; the client never receives credential material; tool results contain no credential

pairs.question: Does a thread that fails partway leave a receipt?
pairs.W0: every POST in the thread succeeds
pairs.W1: POST k > 1 fails after earlier posts succeeded
pairs.D1: receipt, status PARTIAL, and re-dispatch refused
pairs.method: fixture x_request raising on the second POST
pairs.expected_base: W1 writes no receipt: the first post is live and unrecorded, and a second publish attempt is not refused
pairs.expected_fix: W1 writes a PARTIAL row with the ids that were posted, and dispatch refuses that revision until the owner resolves it
